title: introduce-targeted-presubmit-dep-rotation-and-stage-aware-presubmit-orchestration
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: Our presubmit lanes have accumulated a large universe of dependency bumps and full-lane lint runs which lengthen feedback and increase flakiness. Recent incidents during a Dedicated rollout highlighted a transitive dependency mismatch that slips past staged checks because dependency rotation runs are coarse-grained and run infrequently. This PR introduces a targeted dependency rotation mechanism and a stage-aware presubmit orchestration layer that reduces CI noise, speeds feedback for common edits, and ensures dependency updates exercise the same staged lanes used for release candidates.

Summary of changes: 1) Add a small service/runner component (presubmit-orch) that computes a minimal set of lanes to run based on changed paths plus a targeted dependency-rotation plan when package-locks or go.sum change. 2) Implement a dependency-rotation scheduler that runs lightweight upgrade probes (no rebuild) and escalates to full integration lanes only when heuristics indicate high-risk (major semver bump, native deps touched). 3) Split lint/test matrix into: quick (fast local checks + staged path sniffing), staged (per-target integration), and rotation (dependency-only probes). 4) Add new YAML templates and a thin action wrapper so repos can opt-in per-folder. 5) Update docs and GraphQL endpoint used by the PR dashboard for visibility.

Motivation: We want fast turnarounds for typical code changes (sub-10m feedback) while still increasing cadence and coverage of dependency rotation without taxing our full integration infrastructure. This preserves quality for release paths by ensuring dependency updates hit the same staged lanes used for release smoke tests.

What changed (high-level): - presubmit/orchestrator/runner: new orchestrator that inspects changed files and kicks off the minimal lane set. - .github/workflows/presubmit-staged.yml: new template that uses the orchestrator decision. - actions/dep-rotation: action to run targeted dependency probes with heuristics and cacheable probes. - buildkite/ci-templates: updated to allow staged lanes to be triggered by the orchestrator for dedicated runs. - docs/dev/ci-presubmit.md: documentation and opt-in guide.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests for the orchestrator heuristics and integration tests running in the benchmark-lab were added. Ran canary on redwood-examples and redwood-sdk-python for two weeks: median presubmit time for code-only edits dropped from ~18m to ~6m; dependency-rotation increased number of shallow probes by 3x but full integration lane runs remained stable. CI on this branch: initial run had two flaky integration failures; both were traced to timing in a test harness and fixed in follow-up commits. All checks passing at merge.

Migration and opt-in: Default behavior is no-op until repo-level opt-in via .github/presubmit-config.yml. We added an opt-in guide and a migration checklist; platform teams can enable orchestrator per folder, and there is a rollback flag to stop orchestrator-triggered lanes if issues arise.

Risks and mitigations: Risk of missing a necessary integration-run for rare transitive changes mitigated by: 1) rotation heuristics conservative for native or major bumps, 2) nightly full-rotation job retained, and 3) dashboard alerting for any dependency probe failures that would escalate.

Related work: ENG-7249 introduced the initial lane-slicing heuristics; ENG-7310 defines rotation semantics and alerting. SUP-1032 tracked the production dependency incident that motivated this change.

Release notes: introduces targeted dependency rotation and stage-aware presubmit orchestration to speed presubmit feedback and centralize dependency probe logic.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for orchestrator heuristics
- [x] Integration tests for rotation probes
- [x] Canary run on two repositories (redwood-examples, redwood-sdk-python)
- [x] Documentation and opt-in guide
- [x] Rollout plan with rollback flag

Merge notes: Squash merge. Post-merge: deployed orchestrator to the presubmit runner pool and published docs to the internal docs site.

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Nice direction — can we tighten the heuristics for go.sum changes so large transitive bumps trigger immediate full lanes?
Author (Aisha Patel): Done; heuristics now escalate to full lanes for semver-major changes and when native modules are present.
Lena Hoffmann: The new action runner looks heavier than expected; can we make the probe more cache-friendly?
Author (Aisha Patel): Adjusted probe to reuse lockfile diffs and added a local-state cache to reduce repeated resolution work; benchmark shows 40% CPU savings on probes.
Devon Kim: Tests look good; please add a dashboard alert for failed rotation probes so SRE can triage quickly.
Author (Aisha Patel): Added presubmit.rotation_probe_failed alert and documentation to the SRE playbook section.
release_notes: Introduce a stage-aware presubmit orchestrator that reduces presubmit latency by running only the minimal required lanes and a targeted dependency rotation subsystem that increases probe cadence while minimizing full integration runs.
